V-A states 'Runtime latency is measured on a multicore Intel i9 CPU' for inference but does not specify the machine on which MILP was run, nor the MILP solver used, nor absolute wall-clock times per regime; Table I only provides relative speed-up intervals ('≥10×', '15×–20×', '>100×') without the absolute MILP execution times needed to verify these figures.

The paper does report some absolute timing context—“MILP solver shows a strong dependency on graph density, ranging from a few milliseconds in sparse graphs to several hundreds of milliseconds in dense topologies” and “Runtime latency is measured on a multicore Intel i9 CPU (128 GB DDR5 RAM)”—so the claim that times/hardware are entirely absent is overstated. However, the MILP solver itself is not named and Table I gives only interval speed-ups, so the speed-up reporting remains somewhat under-specified.

The reviewer's claim that the paper 'never states the absolute MILP wall-clock times per regime' is factually incorrect. Figure 2 explicitly plots the absolute execution time (in ms) for MILP, Greedy, and L2O as a function of the number of edges, which directly map to the sparsity regimes defined in the text.
